turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Hey, I'm stuck at Line 9, Inspection cell E. ACE shows the i4L-R831 in the Detected Controller IP Address area, but when I hit Connect it just fails with an online connection error.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Alright, what's the controller's IP and subnet right now?

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Controller is 192.168.10.45 with subnet 255.255.255.0, no gateway. My maintenance PC is 192.168.1.20, subnet 255.255.255.0. I already rebooted the PC and reseated the Ethernet cable at the cell E patch panel, but it still won't connect.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Yeah, that's the problem. The controller's on a different LAN and has no gateway, so ACE can detect it but it can't connect online until you change the network settings.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: So should I swap the cable or the controller? I was thinking maybe the controller's bad since it shows up but won't connect.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: No, don't touch the cable or the controller. On Line 9, that inspection cell E controller has to be set to 192.168.1.45/24 with gateway 192.168.1.1 before ACE will connect.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Okay, so change the controller side, not my PC adapter?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Right. If the controller's on a different LAN and has no gateway, you change the controller's IP and subnet first rather than messing with the PC's network adapter.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Got it. Should I log this somewhere before I start changing things?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Always. I check and record the controller subnet and gateway in the Line 9 network log before changing the PC adapter. Do that first.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Makes sense. Did we have this before on Line 9?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Yeah, we had a past incident on Line 9 where a controller on a different VLAN without a gateway was detected but couldn't connect until the controller IP was changed.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: That sounds exactly like this. The new managed switch went in last Friday and my PC got moved to a different VLAN yesterday.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: That'll do it. Set the controller to 192.168.1.45/24 with gateway 192.168.1.1, log it in the Line 9 network log, and then try Connect again.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Hey, I need help with i4L-R186 on Dong Nai Line 1, cell C. ACE is showing an empty Detected Controller IP Address area for it. I clicked Detect and Configure Robotic Controller twice and nothing came up.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Okay, did you look at the lights before opening ACE? I always check the switch power LED and the controller Ethernet port link LED first.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: The controller Ethernet port link LEDs are dark. And when I plug the PC NIC into the cell C patch panel, I get no link light either.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: We put in a new unmanaged switch in the cell C cabinet about two hours ago. Nobody moved or reconfigured the robot controller.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: So if no controller is detected after a switch change, first verify the switch has power and the controller link LED is on. No link light means it's not a software problem.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: So I shouldn't keep clicking Detect and Configure Robotic Controller? I thought maybe it would find it if I tried again.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: No, that button just looks on the Ethernet network. If the port has no link light, it won't find anything no matter how many times you click.

turns.speaker: supervisor_01
turns.text: What's the story here? Are we swapping the controller on i4L-R186 or not?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Hold off on replacing the controller. On Dong Nai Line 1, the cell C unmanaged switch must be powered from the 24 V cabinet supply, not the 5 V USB outlet.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Hmm, the new switch might be on the USB outlet. I didn't check where it was plugged in.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Go check that first. And while you're in there, look at the RJ45 plug too. We had a previous no-detection incident at cell C that was caused by a miswired RJ45 plug after a switch replacement, not by the controller.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Okay, so power the switch from the 24 V cabinet supply, check the switch power LED and the controller link LED, then look at the RJ45 wiring.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Right. Once you get link lights, then open ACE, click Connect to Device, pick the controller from the Detected Controller IP Address area, and hit Connect.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Hey, got a minute? FX5-PLC616 on packaging cell F has been throwing intermittent comms timeouts, three of them between 08:15 and 08:29 this morning.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Timeouts on the simple CPU link again? What's the error code showing in the special device?

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: 0x1F2E, communication timeout. Diagnostics buffer logged it at 08:15, 08:22, and 08:29. HMI showed 'Communications impossible' so I figured maybe the CPU module is going bad — should we swap it?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Don't touch the CPU yet. I always check the simple CPU communication error code in the special device before I even look at a cable — 80% of the intermittent faults we've had on this line came from a busy network segment, not the module.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Okay. But the line ran fine for two weeks after the last parameter change on the 27th of May, so I didn't think parameters were the issue.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: When retries show up like that, first thing I do is review the communication retry count and the time-out period in the simple CPU communication settings. Only after that do I start checking physical cables.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Retry count's sitting at 5. Wait, was that changed at some point?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Yeah, we bumped it from 3 to 5 back in March 2024 after we got similar dropouts during high-traffic periods. So the count itself isn't your problem.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Huh. Also, did you hear the spare-parts delivery got pushed to Thursday? The guys on line 3 are grumbling about it.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Figures. Anyway — wasn't there a new Ethernet switch put in the panel yesterday?

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Yes, an unmanaged one got swapped for a new switch on the 9th. Should be fine though, right?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: We had this exact thing in 2023 when a vision camera was added to the same switch — intermittent dropouts. Separating the camera onto a different VLAN fixed it.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: So you're saying check the line for a busy segment first. Oh, and lunch is at 11:30 today, they moved it because of the shift handover.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Noted. So pull the switch traffic and see what else is sharing that segment with the PLC — I bet you'll find your culprit there.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Hey, I need a hand with MR-JE-AX205 on Line 5. It keeps throwing AL. 17.4, like two or three times a shift, but only when machining cell A is running at high spindle load. I power cycle it and it resets fine, but then it comes back within 30 minutes. No other alarms. Cabinet temp is around 42°C, and they installed a new welding machine about 5 meters away last week.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Alright. Before you even think about swapping the amplifier, did you follow the manual? Disconnect all cables except power and see if the alarm repeats.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Not yet, I wanted to ask you first. I figured it's the amplifier, so maybe we just replace it?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: No, hold on. If it's not repeatable with cables disconnected, the amplifier is probably fine. Then you check for environmental causes. And before replacing anything, I always re-seat the CN1 and CN2 connectors three times to clear oxidation on the pins. That alone has fixed a bunch of these.

turns.speaker: supervisor_01
turns.text: Just to add, we can't afford to swap the amplifier if it's not the root cause. We had a similar intermittent issue on Line 5 back in 2022.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Right, that 2022 case was a welding machine nearby causing AL. 17.4. We added a ferrite core on the 24V line and it fixed it. So with that new welder 5 meters away, that's a strong suspect.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: So you think the welder is interfering? But why would it only happen at high spindle load?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Because at high load, the spindle motor cables are carrying more current. If your 24V control wiring is routed alongside those spindle motor cables in the same duct, that's a classic path for noise. Check your duct routing.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Okay, I'll look at that. What if the alarm doesn't repeat after I disconnect the cables?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Then I check the shield grounding of the encoder cable at the motor end first. Not the encoder itself, not the motor. Just the shield grounding. That's where I start.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Got it. And if it does repeat with cables disconnected?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Then you replace the servo amplifier. But only after you've done the re-seat on CN1 and CN2 and checked the 24V routing. Don't skip steps.

turns.speaker: supervisor_01
turns.text: Good. Let's do the checks and report back before we order any parts. We've got production running.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Hey, got a problem on Line 10. MR-JE-AX451 is showing Ab on the display, and AX452 and AX453 are showing Ab too. Operator powered up Packaging cell F this morning at 06:40 and it came up right away. Cell was off since Friday 22:00 for the weekend shutdown, no hardware changes logged.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Okay, Ab on the first axis and the following ones. What's the history on that SSCNET cable between AX450 and AX451?

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Log says the SSCNET III cable between AX450 and AX451 was last replaced 14 months ago. I was thinking we just swap that cable right away, that's the manual's call for a disconnected cable, right?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: No, don't jump to replacing the cable yet — a loose connector is a separate, quicker check before you go pulling cables. On this line, a weekend cold shutdown often causes the CNIA connector at AX451 to sit about 0.5 mm loose. Reseat that first before you replace anything.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Got it, I'll reseat CNIA. And if that doesn't do it, do we swap the amplifier? AX451 is the one showing Ab first.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: No, don't replace the MR-JE-AX451 amp either — Ab showing on the following axes points to an upstream cause, not a dead amplifier. If reseating CNIA doesn't clear Ab within one power cycle, power-cycle the previous axis, AX450, first.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: AX450 first, okay. Anything else I should know about this cell? Seems like we've had Ab here before.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Yeah — the 2019 retrofit left a spare compatible controller in the cabinet. We swapped to it back in 2022 and it cleared a similar Ab event. Keep that in mind if the reseat and the AX450 power-cycle don't do it.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: There's also the new simple motion module that was installed on the line controller three weeks ago. It ran fine until this weekend though. Could that be involved?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: That's actually a likely culprit. The simple motion module's servo series, Pr.100, was left at default after the March firmware update — it has to be set to the MR-JE series code.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: So Pr.100 is still sitting at default. Should I check that before or after the CNIA reseat?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Do the CNIA reseat first, like I said about the cold shutdown — that's the quickest and it's bit us before. Then if Ab is still there after one power cycle, power-cycle AX450. Check Pr.100 on the motion module while you're at it, since it was left at default after the March firmware update.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Understood. Reseat CNIA, one power cycle, then AX450 power-cycle, and verify Pr.100 is set to the MR-JE series code. If all that fails, swap in the spare compatible controller from the 2019 retrofit.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: That's the order. And remember the cable's only 14 months old, so don't go replacing it unless everything above checks out clean.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Hey, got a weird one on the i4L-R930 in dispensing cell D. Tool sensor readings keep dropping out, maybe three to five times a shift.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Dropping out how? Alarm on the controller?

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: No alarms at all. Robot just keeps moving. The XIO input for the tool sensor flickers, and the scanner throws checksum errors sometimes.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Scanner? So somebody ran serial data through the USER connector pins, didn't they.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Yeah, we added a new cable for the tool-mounted RS-232 barcode scanner. Dropouts started right after that.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: There's your problem. On this cell, tool-side serial data goes through the XBELTIO RS-232 port, not the USER pass-through pins.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Oh. I thought the USER pins were just one-to-one passthrough, so it'd be fine.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: One-to-one, sure, but they've got no twisted pair in them. Manual even says don't use them for data communication. So why would we route an RS-232 scanner through there?

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Makes sense. Should I just swap the sensor then? Maybe it's going bad.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: No, don't waste a sensor. The dropouts showed up right when you added that cable, so it's wiring, not the sensor.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Could we just clamp a ferrite on the USER pass-through cable?

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: I mean, would that help?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Nah. Manual says data communication isn't recommended on those connectors at all. A ferrite's just putting a band-aid on a connector we shouldn't be using for data in the first place.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Okay, so what about the sensor wiring itself? Is that on the USER pins too?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: No. Our 24 VDC tool sensor wiring on this site uses a 0.5 mm² twisted pair from the XIO connector. Not the USER pass-through. Keep those separate.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Got it. Any idea why the flicker got worse lately? We didn't touch the sensor wiring.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Last time we had intermittent tool sensor faults on i4L-R930, it turned out to be induced noise from a nearby servo drive cable that got bundled with the USER pass-through wiring.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: So the new scanner cable is basically running right alongside the drive cable?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Probably. Pull the scanner off the USER pins, reroute it to XBELTIO, and separate that bundle from the drive cable. Then watch it for a shift.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Will do. By the way, did you hear about the shift schedule change next week?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Yeah, they're moving us to the early slot Wednesday. I'm not thrilled about it.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Same. Oh, and the spare-parts delivery for the other line got pushed to Friday.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Of course it did. Figures. Anyway, you grabbing lunch after this?

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Yeah, once I finish tagging the cable. I'll let you know how the reroute looks.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Good. And remember — serial data goes to XBELTIO, sensor stays on the XIO twisted pair, and keep it away from the drive cable.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Got it. Thanks, that saves me from replacing a perfectly good sensor.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Hey, i4L-R957 in cell D is dead in the water. After that power dip it boots up clean, no alarms, but when I hit Start it won't move. Control Power LED is on, High Power LED is off, pendant says High Power OFF, and the safety gate's closed. I already cycled the Control Power switch twice in the last ten minutes.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Don't cycle Control Power again, that won't get you anywhere — it can't move until High Power's actually supplied and enabled, and that needs the safety circuit to be continuous. Before you even think about swapping hardware, walk over and tap the gate switch housing, the one wired into the High Power enable relay. On this unit it sticks open after a power dip, and a light tap seats it back.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Okay, I'll go tap it. If that doesn't do it, should I pull the servo amp?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Not yet. Check the XSYSTEM jumper plug for High Power enable first — ours is a custom shorting plug and it loosens up after thermal cycling, so reseat it before you replace any servo amplifier. And last time this happened on Line 12, back in 2021 after a power dip, the High Power contactor coil failed open. Put a meter on the coil, it should read around 120 ohms, and check that before you go ordering a whole new robot.

turns.speaker: supervisor_01
turns.text: How long is that going to take? We've got the machining cell sitting idle.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Give us fifteen minutes. Tap the gate switch housing first, then reseat the XSYSTEM jumper, then ohm out that contactor coil. If the coil's open, that's your culprit and we order the part — not the amplifier, not the robot.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Got it. Tapped the housing and the High Power LED just came on. So it was the gate switch sticking open the whole time.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: That's the one. Still reseat that jumper plug and check the coil resistance while you're in there, so we don't get surprised next power dip.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Hey, found a 15 mm crack in the J2 bellows on i4L-R446 during the Monday 06:30 check. There's fine cardboard dust packed inside the fold and around the J2 joint. It wasn't there Friday. Should we swap the whole J2 axis before the weekend push?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: No, don't swap the whole J2 axis — the manual calls for bellows replacement, not axis replacement when only the bellows is cracked. Before you judge that crack, wipe the J2 bellows fold with a dry lint-free cloth, because packed dust can look like a split.

turns.speaker: supervisor_01
turns.text: So just the bellows kit then? What's our spare situation looking like?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Keep two spare J2 bellows kits in the Line 5 cabinet because i4L-R446 cracks them about every 6 weeks. And never use organic solvents on the bellows or joint surfaces — dry cloth or mild soap only, solvents will damage the electronics and put us in an unsafe state.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Got it. The dust is really packing in there since the carton erector upstream was replaced two weeks ago.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Yeah, on i4L-R446 that cardboard dust from the new erector reaches J2 in about 10 days, so inspect that bellows every Monday and Thursday now, not just the weekly check.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Monday and Thursday, I'll add it to the route. So I'll wipe it down first, then replace the kit if it's a real split.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Right, like I said about wiping the fold first — dry lint-free cloth before you judge any crack. Then grab one of the two spare kits from the Line 5 cabinet and we're set for the weekend.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Hey, got a weird one on the i4L-R795 in Packaging cell A. J3 position errors, two or three times a shift, mostly after it's been running four hours plus. And I swear I caught a whiff of hot plastic near the base cover.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Hot plastic smell on the i4L-R795, that's usually the J3 encoder connector before the motor ever gets hot. Check the connector first, not the motor.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Yeah but I want to catch it live. Cell's stopped, controller's still energized, so I was just going to pop the base cover and wiggle the J3 encoder cable and watch the error come up.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: No, don't do that — you never connect or disconnect system cables with power on, and those covers aren't interlocked, so power comes off and gets disconnected before the cover comes off. Lock out and tag out first, and on Packaging cell A lock out the upstream case sealer too, because pallet backlog can push into the cell.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Okay, okay. Oh — did you hear the spares delivery got pushed to Thursday? Half the line's waiting on it.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Figures. Look, before you even think about replacing the encoder, check the shield clamp — a loose shield clamp is what usually causes J3 encoder faults on this machine, so check the clamp screw torque first.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: And if the clamp torque is fine? Do we have a spare cable or am I ordering one?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: There's a spare J3 encoder cable in the Line 4 spares bin — keep one there, because i4L-R795 has already had two cable failures since January. Now go grab lunch before the canteen closes.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Hey, I'm doing the weekly safety check on i4L-R496 over in Palletizing cell D, Line 10. Control Power's on and High Power was disabled, but when I request High Power the indicator never flashes. I tried it three times, still nothing. No alarms on the log and it ran fine for eight hours before this.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Okay, first thing before you touch anything: lock out the robot's main disconnect and wait 30 seconds for the DC bus to discharge. Don't go poking at connectors with that bus still live.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Got it, I'll lock it out and wait. So should I just swap the High Power LED? That seems like the obvious culprit.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: No, don't jump to the LED. On this unit a stuck High Power indicator usually traces to a loose connector J12 behind the Primary Interface Panel, not a failed LED. Also, always verify by requesting High Power twice with a 5-second pause between, because the first request after a cold start may not register.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Alright, I'll do the double request with the pause. If it still doesn't flash after that, what then?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Check J12 first. And keep in mind back in 2023 this same machine had a similar symptom that turned out to be a faulty 24V fuse F3 on the interface board. So after you've checked the connector, if it's still dead, that fuse is the next thing to replace.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Understood, I'll check J12 then the F3 fuse. And I won't just skip the check since the robot was running fine.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Right, don't ignore it. That indicator has to flash after a High Power request for the check to pass, so let's find the real cause.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Hey, I need help with the MR-JE-AX276 on Palletizing cell B, Line 12. AL.13 keeps popping up, like two or three times a shift.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Clock error, right? Does it come back after you cycle the power?

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Yeah, it clears but then it's back within ten, fifteen minutes of running the cycle. And no other axes on the same controller are alarming.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: We just replaced the encoder cable on that axis last week, didn't we? Started the next day?

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Exactly. So I was thinking, manual says it's either the amplifier internal failure or a clock signal from the controller. Should I just swap the MR-JE out?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Hold on. On Line 12, AL.13 on axis 276 has historically been a loose CN1 connector, not the amplifier itself. Before you replace the MR-JE-AX276, always reseat the CN1 and CN3 connectors and recheck. That's fixed four of the last five AL.13 cases on Palletizing cell B.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Okay, so reseat CN1 and CN3 first. And if it still alarms after that?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Then swap the amplifier with the identical spare from the Line 12 cabinet before you order a new unit. Don't jump straight to a new one.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Got it. What about the repeatability test the manual mentions, disconnecting cables?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: When you do that, leave the 24 V control power on so you can still pull the alarm log through MR Configurator2. Otherwise you lose the history.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Makes sense. So I shouldn't assume the controller is bad either, since only axis 276 is alarming?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Right. Other axes on that controller run fine, so don't touch the PLC. Reseat the connectors, and if it persists, try the spare amp.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Hey, need your help. The FX5-PLC724 at Pick-and-place cell B tripped at 06:42, HMI showed 7D02H. I restarted twice and it came back within 20 seconds both times, and once I also saw 7D12H flash up. Yesterday evening someone edited the predefined protocol settings for the barcode scanner on channel 2 and downloaded before handover. I read SD9102 as 0 and the SD9132-SD9135 registration monitor doesn't show the scanner protocol number at all.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Don't swap the CPU yet. On the FX5-PLC724 here at Dong Nai, SD9102 stays 0 for about 8 seconds after power-up, so your S(P).CPRTCL instruction has to be gated by an SD9102 rising-edge contact. That alone explains a lot of these morning trips.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Okay, but the registration monitor is empty for the scanner. Did the download wipe it, or is the protocol number just wrong?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: The scanner protocol on cell B was renumbered from 3 to 5 during the March 2024 retrofit, and the old backup files still carry protocol 3. So if someone pulled yesterday's edit from an old backup, they downloaded protocol 3 and the cell is looking for 5. Also, before you rewrite any protocol setting data on this FX5-PLC724, always save the current SD9132-SD9135 registration map to the maintenance laptop first.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Got it. And what about the 7D12H that showed up once? Should I go straight into the protocol data, or check cabling?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: If 7D02H shows up together with 7D12H on this cell, reseat the CH2 RS-485 cable at the scanner junction box before you touch any protocol data. Do that first, then save the SD9132-SD9135 map on the laptop, then rewrite the protocol setting data and rerun the instruction.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: One of the other guys said we should just clear all the protocol registrations and start from an empty config. That sound right?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: No, don't do that. Clearing everything removes the scanner protocol number and you'll get 7D10H instead of fixing 7D02H. Just gate the S(P).CPRTCL with the SD9102 rising edge, reseat that CH2 cable, save the registration map, and rewrite the protocol data with protocol 5.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Hey, I need a hand with i4L-R262 in the dispensing cell C at Line 1. It's been drifting about 0.5 mm on the X axis after roughly 20 minutes of production.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Drifting on X, huh. Any alarm codes come up?

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: No alarms at all. The vision system caught it and rejected three parts in a row. I did a visual check and found the Joint 2 hardstop screw loose after about 200 hours of operation. Last adjusted two weeks ago during PM.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Yeah, that fits. On the i4L-R262, a loose Joint 2 hardstop screw often causes gradual drift that mimics servo tuning issues. People chase the servo and miss the actual problem.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: So it's not the motor then? I was thinking maybe the encoder's failing since it only shows up after it warms up.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Don't swap the motor yet. And don't just bump the servo gain to hide the drift either, that'll bite you later. Check the hardstop screw first.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Okay. What's the right way to redo it so it actually holds this time?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Clean the screw and the hole with isopropyl alcohol first, then apply Loctite 243. Only after it's clean. And use a calibrated torque wrench, tighten to 17 N-m.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Got it. Should I check it again after a while, or is once enough?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Always re-check the hardstop screw torque after the first 50 hours of operation. Thermal cycling can relax the thread lock, so it needs a follow-up.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Makes sense. Has this happened before on these machines?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Back in 2019 here at Plant Dong Nai, someone omitted the thread lock on the Joint 2 hardstops. It drifted 2 mm and crashed within 8 hours.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Wow. Okay, I'll clean it, torque it to 17 N-m with the Loctite 243, and come back at 50 hours to re-check.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: That's the way. And if you still see drift after that, then we start looking at the servo.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Hey, I've got a problem on Line 1, Packaging cell A. The FX5-PLC140 ERR LED was blinking red at 1 Hz around 14:20 after a brief network dropout, so I power-cycled it at 14:25. Now it's solid red and the HMI lost communication with the PLC.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: You power-cycled it? Ah, that's the thing — on the FX5-PLC140 at Packaging cell A, always clear network errors with GX Works3 Ethernet diagnostics before power-cycling. Power-cycling can latch the error and you lose the event log.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: I didn't know that. GX Works3 is showing error code 0x1A01 in the module diagnostics, but I couldn't clear it with the LED reset procedure.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: 0x1A01 again. We've had three similar ones here caused by a loose RJ45 connector on the cell switch port 4. Check that connector first.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Okay, I'll check port 4. Should I try Ethernet diagnostics in GX Works3 now?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Yes. And if Ethernet diagnostics can't connect, use the USB programming port with GX Works3 to read and clear the error without stopping the line.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Got it. By the way, did the spare-parts delivery come in for the other line?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: No, still waiting on that. It's supposed to arrive after lunch tomorrow.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Alright. So after I clear 0x1A01, is there anything else to confirm before I restart the cell?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: After clearing error 0x1A01, verify the link LED on the FX5-PLC140 Ethernet port is solid green for 30 seconds before restarting the cell.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Solid green for 30 seconds, got it. I reseated the RJ45 on port 4 and it clicked in — it was a bit loose.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Good. Read the error history while you're in there too — the event history shows more detail than just the LEDs, so you can see what actually triggered it.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Will do. I'll clear it through Ethernet diagnostics and watch that link LED.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Perfect. Let me know if it latches again — and next time, diagnostics before power cycle.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Hey, I've got a weird one on i4L-R472 at Plant Hanoi, Line 11, Assembly cell F. It keeps missing the down position, and the Z height is varying by about a millimeter.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: No alarm code shows up. But the assembly force monitor logs low-force errors now and then. It started right after we adjusted the Joint 3 hardstop during the last maintenance.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Let me guess — did you check the Joint 3 hardstop clamp collar? On the i4L-R472, the z-axis brake has to be engaged before you loosen that clamp collar, or the quill can drop on you suddenly.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: I think the brake was released when we did it. And yeah, the clamp collar slipped about 2 mm down the z-axis quill after only 50 cycles.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: A slipping clamp collar is usually from insufficient torque. Always verify it with a calibrated torque wrench — it needs 4.5 N-m on the socket-head screw.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Could the brake release timing be off? Maybe that's what's causing the height variation.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: No, don't chase the brake release timing for that. The height variation is the collar slipping, not the brake. Also, remember the manual says never loosen or remove that clamp collar with the z-axis brake released.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Okay. Should I just replace the whole z-axis quill assembly to be safe?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Not yet. First check the collar torque and inspect the quill surface for scoring. If the collar is worn, replace the collar itself — no need to swap the whole quill assembly.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Got it. And when I reposition it, do I add anything to the screw?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Yes, after you position the clamp collar, apply thread lock and tighten the socket-head screw to 4.5 N-m.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Is there anything special about this cell? It's been fine for months.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Assembly cell F here at Plant Hanoi has a history of clamp collar slippage from vibration. That's why we re-check the torque every 100 hours on this cell.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Alright, I'll torque it properly, inspect for scoring, and set the 100-hour re-check. Thanks.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Hey, I replaced the servo amplifier on MR-JE-AX893 at Plant Hanoi, Line 4, Assembly cell F, and now the PLC Modbus master is showing a communication timeout when it tries to read the servo status. The amplifier shows no alarm, and the motor runs fine in test mode from the front panel. The new amplifier's rotary switch is set to 0, but the old one was set to 3. The PLC queries station 3 at 19200 baud, 8 data bits, even parity, 1 stop bit.

turns.speaker: supervisor_01
turns.text: Before we dig into that, did you get the spare-parts delivery confirmation for the other line? They were supposed to drop off those sensors this morning.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: No, I haven't checked yet. But about the servo, I was thinking maybe the new amplifier is defective since it's not responding, so should I just swap it out again?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: No, don't replace the amplifier again — the manual says incorrect protocol or station number settings commonly cause this. When replacing an MR-JE amplifier, always copy the old rotary switch position and Pr. PC70 before power-up; mismatch causes silent communication failure. Also, before adjusting parameters, verify the CN3 communication cable is fully seated and the shield is grounded at the amplifier end only. In 2022, a similar communication loss on Line 4 was caused by a loose CN3 connector after maintenance, not by parameter settings.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Okay, so I should check the CN3 connector first. But what about the PLC program? Should I change it to match the new amplifier's rotary switch setting of 0?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: No, don't change the PLC program to match the new amplifier's rotary switch setting of 0 — the manual requires matching the query message station number to the amplifier setting, not altering the master. At Plant Hanoi, Line 4, the PLC Modbus master uses a 100 ms timeout; if no response within that, it flags a fault and does not retry until power cycle. So fix the amplifier side, not the PLC.

turns.speaker: supervisor_01
turns.text: Alright, let's get that CN3 checked and the rotary switch set to 3. Also, don't forget lunch is at noon today, and we have the shift handover at 2 PM.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Like I said about copying the old rotary switch position and Pr. PC70 before power-up, make sure you set the rotary switch to 3 and check Pr. PC70 matches. Once that's done and CN3 is secure, power cycle the PLC to clear the fault.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Hey, I need your help with MR-JE-AX548 on cell D. Alarm F0.3 keeps popping up, like 3 to 5 times a shift, and it started after we re-greased the X-axis ball screw and re-tightened the coupling during last weekend's PM.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Okay, and does it stop the line?

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: No, it clears itself in about 2 seconds and the axis keeps running. I pulled the history with MR Configurator2 and the resonance suppression filter value is different between morning and afternoon logs. I was thinking maybe the motor is going bad?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: No, don't touch the motor. On cell D, before you even think about filter parameters, check the four M4 screws of the X-axis ball screw nut bracket with a torque wrench at 2.5 Nm.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: The bracket screws? Why those first?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Because we had this exact same F0.3 pattern on cell D back in March 2023, and it turned out to be a loose motor mounting bolt, not the servo tuning. So check the mechanical side before you chase the filter.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Got it. And if the bracket screws are tight, then what?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: If they're tight, then lock the notch filter by setting parameter PB13 to 2250 Hz on MR-JE-AX548. Don't leave adaptive tuning active, that's what's letting the filter value drift between logs.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Should I just disable the tough drive function so F0.3 stops showing up? It's not stopping production anyway.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: No, don't do that. F0.3 is telling you there's a real machine resonance, you have to fix it by setting the filter and checking the machine, not by silencing the warning.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Okay, so after I tighten the bracket, how do I know it's actually good?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Always jog the X axis at 10 mm/s by hand after tightening the bracket and feel for a mechanical catch before you put it back in automatic mode.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Alright, I'll torque the four M4 bracket screws to 2.5 Nm first, then jog it slow, and if everything's tight I'll set PB13 to 2250 Hz. Thanks.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: That's the order. And remember the March 2023 one was a loose motor mounting bolt, so if the bracket's fine, don't forget to look there too.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Hey, I need a sanity check. On i4L-R518, Packaging cell E, I saw two switches on the Primary Interface Panel set different from what the maintenance log says. The robot's running fine, no alarms, but I spent 45 minutes trying to match them to the log. I'm worried we have a hidden fault.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Don't worry about it — that panel's a dead end. Those switches have been unused since installation; there's no wiring connected to them at all.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: No wiring? So they don't do anything? But the log lists them as adjustable parameters, so I figured they must matter for safety or something.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Yeah, the site's maintenance log for i4L-R518 is wrong on that — it lists switch positions as adjustable parameters. That's what causes this confusion every few months.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: And listen — do not adjust any switch on the Primary Interface Panel. They're just placeholders, and moving them can break the plastic detents. Last time someone kept flipping one, we had to replace the whole panel cover.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Got it, I'll leave them alone. So if someone reports a switch position discrepancy, what should I do?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Show them the manual excerpt — it says those positions are reserved for future use and have no impact on robot functionality. Then update the log to mark switches as 'reserved – do not touch'.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: That makes sense. By the way, did you see the shift schedule change for next week? We're swapping to nights on Thursday.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Yeah, I saw that. I'm on days still, but I think the spare-parts delivery for the other line is coming Thursday too, so we'll have to juggle.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Okay, I'll keep an eye out. So to be clear: the switches on i4L-R518 are placeholders, the log is wrong, and I shouldn't touch them.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Exactly. And if the log still confuses people, just mark them as 'reserved – do not touch' so nobody wastes another 45 minutes.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Will do. Thanks — I'll grab lunch after I update that log entry.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Morning, need you at Palletizing cell D on Line 3. The MR-JE-AX549 servo amplifier shows no alarm at all, nothing on the 7-segment, but the palletizing axis just sits there locked and humming when I give a jog.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Okay, don't touch the jog yet. First thing on this cell, the 24 VDC brake supply comes from breaker QF12 in panel P3. If QF12 is off, the brake never releases and the motor just hums like that.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: QF12... the panel was cleaned over the weekend and we powered everything down. Let me look. Yeah, the brake release LED on the local brake supply is off and I read 0 VDC at the brake terminals.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: That's your problem then. Someone left QF12 off after the panel cleaning. But before you just flip it and force a jog, I always verify brake release first — listen for the click at the motor and check the shaft turns by hand with the servo off.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Got it. So I shouldn't just replace the MR-JE-AX549? I mean the motor hums and doesn't move, I thought maybe the amplifier was gone.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: No, don't swap the amplifier. The manual says check the brake power supply first, and that's exactly what QF12 is. A hum with no movement and no alarm is the brake holding, not the amp.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Alright. Should I be worried about the SP1, SP2, SP3 speed selections too? I saw those in the manual.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Those only matter in speed or torque mode when the wrong SP selection gives a bad speed command. They can't explain a shaft you can't turn by hand with the servo off, so leave them alone until the brake actually releases.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Makes sense. One more thing — before I flip QF12, is there anything else on this cell that's bitten us before?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Yeah, back in 2022 on this same cell we had a loose brake connector right at the motor, not the amplifier. So check that connector first while you're down there, then turn QF12 on.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Connector's seated fine. I'm turning QF12 on now... LED's lit, I hear the click at the motor, and the shaft turns by hand with servo off. We're good.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Good. Now jog it at 10% speed for 30 seconds to confirm smooth release before you hand it back to production. Don't go straight to full speed.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Jogging at 10%... axis moving smooth, no hum. I'll run the 30 seconds and then call the operator back.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Perfect. And next time, after any panel work, check QF12 before you even think about the amplifier.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Hey, I'm stuck on MR-JE-AX824 in Dispensing Cell A, Line 5. Alarm 36.1 keeps popping up about every 70 milliseconds during the dispensing cycle, even though I reseated the SSCNET III cable connector at the servo amp yesterday.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Okay, first thing—don't swap the amplifier yet. On Line 5, the vibration from the dispensing cell is known to loosen the SSCNET connector. Did you check the connector locking tab?

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: I pushed it in until it clicked, but I didn't really look at the tab. I just assumed it was seated. Should I pull the amp and replace it?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: No, not yet. The manual lists cable disconnection, dirty tips, and plasticizer contamination as earlier checks. Replacing the amp now would be jumping the gun. Go back and actually inspect that locking tab.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Alright, I'll check the tab. But what about the cable? There's a bundle of wires zip-tied with vinyl tape running right next to the moving robot arm.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: That vinyl tape is a red flag. Three months ago we had a similar intermittent alarm on MR-JE-AX824, and it turned out to be plasticizer migration from a nearby PVC wire bundle. The plasticizer leaches into the SSCNET cable and messes with the signal.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: So the tape itself could be causing it? I thought dirty cable tips were the main issue. The cabinet hasn't been cleaned in about 1,200 hours.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Dirty tips can cause continuous communication errors, but your alarm is intermittent—every 70 milliseconds or so. That points more to vibration or contamination. Before you even think about replacing the servo amp, clean the SSCNET cable tip with isopropyl alcohol and then retest for a full 30 minutes.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Got it, clean the tip and run it for 30 minutes. What about the cable routing? Should I just re-zip-tie it with the same vinyl tape?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: No, keep at least 50 mm separation between the SSCNET cable and any PVC-insulated power cables in the cable tray. That plasticizer migration happens when they're too close. Use a proper separator or route it away from the power bundle.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Okay, I'll move it and check the locking tab. But what if the alarm still comes back after all that? Could the controller be faulty?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Don't jump to the controller either. The manual says to check the SSCNET cable and adjacent amplifiers before blaming the controller. Start with the cable tip cleaning, the tab, and the separation. Then retest.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Understood. I'll clean the tip with isopropyl alcohol, check the locking tab, separate the cables by at least 50 mm, and run it for 30 minutes. Then I'll report back.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: That's the right order. And remember, last time on MR-JE-AX824 it was that plasticizer migration from the PVC bundle. So pay attention to any vinyl tape or PVC insulation near the SSCNET cable.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Hey, I need a hand. The FX5-PLC712 over at Palletizing cell C keeps throwing error C1CDH on the HMI.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: C1CDH, that's the SLMPSND send failure. When did it start?

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: 14:22. It came up three times in ten minutes, and every time it's right in the palletizing cycle when we send position data to the warehouse PC.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Three times in ten minutes, huh. Is the warehouse PC still talking to the other devices on that switch?

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Yeah, everything else on the switch is fine. Only our PLC's send is failing.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: On this line, C1CDH usually shows up when the warehouse PC's TCP receive buffer is full. Restart the data logger service on that PC and it clears right up.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Just restart the service? Not the whole PC?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Just the service. Last time this happened on Line 11 I spent an hour chasing the cable before I figured that out.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Okay, I'll try that. Anything else I should look at while I'm over there?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Didn't you guys just replace the Ethernet cable from the PLC to the hub after the forklift hit the cabinet?

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Yeah, last week. The cable looks fine though.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: After any cable replacement on cell C, always check the RJ45 clip is fully seated, and give the cable a tug-test at both ends. A loose clip causes intermittent send failures exactly like this.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Got it. I'll check both ends. What about the switch itself?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: The switching hub in cabinet C is unmanaged, and its port 3 has a history of intermittent link drops. Move the PLC over to port 5.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Port 3 to port 5, okay. Should I swap the CPU module too? It's been in there a while.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: No, don't touch the CPU. C1CDH is a send failure, it's almost always the external device or the network, not the PLC hardware.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Good, I didn't want to pull a CPU if I didn't have to.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: And don't just ignore it and keep retrying the SLMPSND either. If you don't check the warehouse PC or the switch, it'll just keep failing and you'll lose production time.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Right. And if it keeps coming back after all that?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: If C1CDH repeats more than twice in an hour, put a 50 millisecond delay before the SLMPSND instruction as a temporary workaround.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: A 50 ms delay before the send. That'll hold us until we find the root cause?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Yeah, it's just a band-aid. But it keeps the line running while you sort the PC and the cabling.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Okay, so restart the data logger service, tug-test the cable, move the PLC to port 5, and add the delay if it keeps repeating.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: That's the order. Let me know what you find.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Hey, I need your help. MR-JE-AX636 on Line 12, Assembly cell D, has been showing F5.3 since Monday morning. It comes up right after power-up. Night shift loaded new cam data Friday at 22:15 and powered down at 22:30. The alarm came back twice after two power cycles, and the machine won't run its cam profile. If I don't use cam data, it powers up fine.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: F5.3 is cam data checksum. Before you swap anything, rewrite the cam data, then cycle power. But first, on MR-JE-AX636 at Da Nang, always verify the cam data checksum in MR Configurator2 before cycling power after a Friday write.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Okay, so don't replace the amplifier yet? I was about to grab a spare from the cage because it says checksum error. Also, I thought maybe the encoder cable was bad — should I swap that too?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: No, don't touch the encoder cable. F5.3 is specifically cam data checksum mismatch, not encoder feedback. And don't replace the amplifier first — the manual says rewrite the cam data and cycle power. By the way, did you eat? I'm heading to the canteen after this.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Not yet. I'll eat after we fix this. So just rewrite and power cycle? I already did that once and it came back.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: We had this exact thing in 2023. A 22:15 Friday cam data write on Line 12 got corrupted by a voltage sag during the weekend, and that caused F5.3. So verify the checksum in MR Configurator2 after the write — before you cycle power.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Got it. Also, the spare-parts delivery for Line 9 is late again — they're saying Thursday now. Anyway, if I rewrite and it still repeats, then what?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: If F5.3 repeats after a clean rewrite, check the 24 V control power supply for noise from the nearby welding cell before replacing the amplifier. That welding cell kicks in around 07:30 and can put noise on the 24 V.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Okay. And do I need to change any parameter before the rewrite? I don't want to mess up the cam data initialization.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Yes — local parameter PT34 for cam data initialization must be set to 1 on MR-JE-AX636 before any cam data rewrite during production. Set that first, then rewrite, then verify checksum in MR Configurator2, then cycle power.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: PT34 to 1, rewrite, verify checksum, cycle power. If it still faults, check 24 V for welding noise. I'll do that now. You going to lunch soon?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Yeah, after I check on Line 7 — they've got a different issue. Let me know what the checksum says before you power cycle. And don't forget PT34.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Will do. Thanks. I'll message you the checksum result.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Hey, I need your help with the dispensing axis on Line 1, cell E. The MR-JE-AX481 servo amp is overshooting about 8% when it moves from 0 to 300 mm at 400 mm/s.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Okay, when did this start? Was anything changed on the line recently?

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Yeah, last week we bumped the line speed from 250 to 400 mm/s. The overshoot started right after that. No alarms on the amp, and the velocity waveform on MR Configurator2 shows a clear peak above the command before it settles.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Alright. On this dispensing cell, overshoot above 5% at 400 mm/s is usually caused by the torque limit being left at 150% from the previous lower-speed setup.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: So you think the torque limit is the issue? I was about to re-run auto tuning with the default response to see if that fixes it.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Don't do that yet. Before touching gain parameters, always verify the torque limit in parameter PA21 on MR-JE-AX481. It was set to 150% during the 2023 speed increase.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Got it, PA21. Should I check the instantaneous torque display too?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Yes, check the torque waveform in MR Configurator2 to confirm it's hitting that limit. But also know that the auto tuning response on this axis was manually fixed at 12 to avoid resonance with the dispenser frame, so re-running auto tuning alone will not fix overshoot.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Oh, I didn't know it was locked at 12. So even if I re-run auto tuning, it won't help because of the frame resonance?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Exactly. The response is fixed at 12 for a reason. If you change it, you'll get vibration. So leave that alone and focus on the torque limit first.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Okay, so I'll check PA21. If it's at 150%, should I just lower it?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Yes, bring it down to a reasonable value for 400 mm/s. Usually around 120% works for this axis. But when adjusting gain, change one parameter at a time and wait 30 seconds for the servo to stabilize before judging the waveform.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: One at a time, 30 seconds. Got it. So I shouldn't touch the gain parameters until I've fixed the torque limit?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Right. The torque limit is the root cause here. Once you set PA21 correctly, the overshoot should drop below 5%. If it doesn't, then we can look at fine-tuning the gain, but only one parameter at a time.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Understood. I'll check PA21 now and set it to 120% if it's at 150. Then I'll watch the waveform for 30 seconds before making any other changes.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Good. And remember, don't re-run auto tuning. That response is fixed at 12 for a reason. Just adjust the torque limit and verify.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Will do. Thanks for the help. I'll let you know how it goes.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: No problem. If you see any other issues, give me a shout.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: At 14:20 today on Line 2, Dispensing cell B, the HMI showed 'No communication' for the MR-JE-AX908 and the servo wouldn't respond to start commands. The link device — cyclic communication ready — was OFF on the PLC side, but the control command was still ON.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: I found the Ethernet cable at CN1 slightly loose, reseated it, and communication came back for about 10 minutes, then dropped again at 14:35. No alarm or warning code on the servo amp either time. I was thinking we should just swap out the servo amplifier.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: No, don't replace the amplifier yet — on Line 2, always check CN1 cable strain relief first. That dispensing cell B robot drags the cable and loosens the connector about once per month.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: We had a past intermittent fault on MR-JE-AX908 between 14:00 and 15:00 that turned out to be a damaged Ethernet cable near the cable carrier, not IP parameters. And don't go toggling Pr. PN31 through PN34 — this site uses those for the PLC IP 192.168.1.10, so if they're unchanged, leave them alone.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: So how do I prove it's the cable and not the parameters?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Quick verification: ping the designated operation IP address from the PLC while a colleague wiggles the CN1 cable. If the ping drops, that confirms it's cable or connector, not a parameter error.

turns.speaker: supervisor_01
turns.text: Can we get that ping test going before the next batch starts?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Yeah, and like I said about the strain relief, check that damaged section near the cable carrier too — that's where the drag happens.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Hey, got a minute? FX5-PLC442 over on Packaging cell C is throwing C431H on the Ethernet diagnostics window. The SP.ECPRTCL to the barcode scanner failed three times in a row in about two minutes.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: C431H means the connection got closed while SP.ECPRTCL was running. Before you touch anything, pull up the connection open status in the Ethernet diagnostics window and check it there, not just the physical cable. And don't go swapping the cable yet, the scanner's probably fine.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Scanner power LED is on and the cable's plugged in. I was gonna swap the Ethernet cable and maybe reset the CPU module first.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Nah, skip the reset and skip the cable. That scanner on cell C has a known firmware quirk, it drops the connection if you send SP.ECPRTCL within 500 ms of the previous one. So space your retries out. Anyway, did the spare-parts guy drop off those rollers for Line 9 yet?

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Not yet, he said after lunch. So if C431H comes back after I reopen the connection, what then?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Then power-cycle the barcode scanner first, then the PLC. Wait 10 seconds between each. That clears it almost every time.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Got it. I'll reopen the connection and retry with a gap. You still on for the 2 pm shift handover?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Yeah, I'll be there after I look at line 10 filler. Just remember, check the connection open status in the diagnostics window before you re-execute, every time.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Hey, got a minute? Night shift flagged event code C056 on FX5-PLC153 out on Line 3, Palletizing cell F. Came up at 02:14 and again at 03:47, each one cleared itself after about 90 seconds.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: C056 again on that cell. Did the robot actually stop, or was it just the alarm?

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Robot stopped mid-cycle both times. No mechanical fault found, nothing jammed, no servo errors. Just the comms alarm.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Okay. Before you even think about touching a cable, pull up the C056 detail on FX5-PLC153 and check the parameter storage location and the I/O number. That tells you which parameter it's really complaining about.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: The parameter storage location and I/O number, got it. I was honestly about to just swap the CPU module first.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: No, don't do that. C056 is a minor Ethernet parameter error, the manual lists it as a communication error with parameter info, not an MPU or memory failure. Swapping the CPU is just burning money.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Fair enough. It's self-clearing anyway, some guys were saying maybe just ignore it.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Ignoring it is worse. That parameter info points to one specific Ethernet parameter you need to correct, otherwise it keeps coming back. It's not noise.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: And log it properly first. Write the exact C056 timestamp and the parameter item number in the shift log before you clear the alarm. Once you clear it, that detail's gone.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Exact timestamp and the parameter item number, before clearing. Okay.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: By the way, did the spare M12 cables come in? The ones I ordered for the camera drops.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Not yet, warehouse said Thursday. Oh, and they added a new vision camera to that same Ethernet segment three days ago. Could that be it?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Maybe. Last time we had C056 recurring on Line 3 was back in 2021, and that one turned out to be a loose M12 connector at the vision camera drop. Nothing wrong with the PLC at all.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: So check the camera drop connector, not the PLC.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Right. And while you're diagnosing, temporarily set the cell F Ethernet link speed to 100 Mbps full duplex. It stabilizes the segment so the alarm stops flapping while you hunt.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: 100 Mbps full duplex, temporary. The switch in panel F was rebooted 11 days ago for the power window, if that matters.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Noted, but the link speed setting is the quick stabilizer. Speaking of the power window, did you eat yet? I skipped lunch, the canteen closed early.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: No, I grabbed a banh mi before shift. You want me to run the checks on cell F now or after the palletizer finishes this batch?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: After the batch, no point stopping mid-pallet. Just don't let it run all night without logging that C056 detail.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Understood. And Line 2's labeler is still throwing that intermittent barcode reject, by the way. Separate issue but same shift.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: We'll look at that after. For now, camera drop connector first, then the link speed, then the log entries. Order matters.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Camera drop, link speed, log. I'll go pull the C056 detail now.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Good. And remind me to follow up on that M12 order, if Thursday slips we're doing this again next week.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Hey, need your brain on something. MR-JE-AX389 over at Packaging cell F on Line 3 tripped AL. 34.1 three times during the 06:15 to 14:15 shift, roughly every 40 minutes. It clears on a power cycle, runs fine for a while, then the 34.1 detail comes back.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Okay. Anything change around that cell lately? Cable routing, trays, anything like that?

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Yeah, actually. The SSCNET III cable was re-routed last week when they put in a new cable tray above the cell. And I measured 41 degrees Celsius near the amplifier cabinet on the last trip.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Good, that helps. On Line 3 the first thing I always do is flex the SSCNET III cable by hand at both connector ends. A broken conductor inside intact insulation shows up exactly like this, intermittent 34.1.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: So you're saying the cable can be bad even though the outside looks perfect?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Exactly. The jacket looks fine but the conductor's cracked inside. Flex it right at both ends and watch for the alarm flickering. That re-route last week is a red flag too.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Somebody suggested just swapping the amplifier, MR-JE-AX389, since they figure the amp is the most likely failed part. Should we do that?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: No, don't jump to replacing the amp. Before you replace MR-JE-AX389, swap the SSCNET cable over to the adjacent axis amplifier and see whether the 34.1 follows the cable.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: So if the alarm moves with the cable, the amp's fine.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Right. If it stays on the same amp, then you look at the amp. But nine times out of ten on this line it's the cable.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: What about cleaning the cable tip with solvent and re-seating it? One of the guys was going to try that.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Don't just clean the tip and re-seat it without checking the routing and the neighboring amplifiers. That's how you waste a shift and the alarm comes right back.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Okay, so what else should I be looking at on the routing?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Look at what's touching the SSCNET cable. Back in 2019 we had the same 34.1 pattern on Hanoi Line 2, and it turned out to be plasticizer migration from a PVC wire bundle that was touching the SSCNET cable.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Plasticizer migration? So the PVC bundle actually degrades the cable.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Yeah, the plasticizer migrates out of the PVC and gets onto the SSCNET cable, and that messes with the signal. So check for any PVC bundle resting against it, especially after a re-route.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Got it. And if I suspect the cable, how do we handle it without a long stop?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Keep a spare 5 m SSCNET III cable in the cell F cabinet. That way if you suspect the cable you can swap it within one production stop.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Nice, that's quick. So my plan is flex both ends first, check for the PVC bundle touching it, then swap the cable to the adjacent amp to see if 34.1 follows.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: That's the order. Flex both ends, check the routing, then the swap test. The spare in the cabinet makes the swap painless.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: And the 41 degrees near the cabinet, is that a concern?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: It's warm but that's not what's causing 34.1. Focus on the cable and the routing. Heat like that you note, but it's not your fault here.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Okay. One more thing, the alarm clears on a power cycle and runs normal for a while before it comes back. That fits a broken conductor, right?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Yeah, that's classic intermittent. Power cycle resets it, vibration or the machine moving flexes that broken conductor, and 34.1 comes back.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Alright, I'll go flex both ends and check what's touching that cable, then do the swap test to the adjacent amp.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Good. Report back what you find. And make sure that spare 5 m SSCNET III cable is stocked in the cell F cabinet for next time.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Hey, got a weird one on MR-JE-AX762, pick-and-place cell F on Line 2. Operator says the rotation speed is fluctuating about plus or minus 15 rpm during constant-speed moves, three or four times a shift, and it started after the controller firmware update last week. No alarm on the amplifier, load looks normal, brake releases fine.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Before you go swapping anything, no, don't just replace the servo motor with a spare — that encoder-failure hunch doesn't fit here. No alarm, normal load, and the manual points at gain or an unstable command from the controller, not the motor. Let's check the command side first.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: So what do you want me to look at first? Should I bump Pr. PA09 up to see if auto tuning response fixes it?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: No, don't do that either — and never adjust Pr. PA09 while the cell is in automatic production. Stop the line and switch to manual first, because changing it live can cause unexpected motion. Also, on this cell Pr. PA09 was set to 18 back in 2022 to reduce vibration, so pushing it higher usually just makes the speed ripple worse.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Okay, so check the command side first. What exactly am I looking for?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Grab MR Configurator2 and trend the command frequency ripple before you touch any gain — if you see about a 5 Hz ripple, that points to the controller, not the servo. And check the command cable connector at the controller end first, because a loose CN1 shield gave us the exact same speed instability on Line 2 back in March.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Got it. So CN1 shield at the controller, then trend the ripple in Configurator2, and leave PA09 alone for now.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Right, like I said about the connector — check that CN1 shield before anything else, since it's the cheapest and it already bit us in March. If the shield's fine, then trend the command frequency ripple; a 5 Hz ripple means we go after the controller, not the servo.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Hey, MR-JE-AX196 on Line 3 is tripping AL.24 about 8 seconds after power-on, three times this morning. It clears on a power cycle but comes right back on servo-on, and if I leave the motor power connector unplugged, no alarm. Yesterday we ran a 6-hour shift in humid weather and I saw condensation on the cabinet door this morning.

turns.speaker: supervisor_01
turns.text: Alright, before you guys dig in, just remember we still need the cell back up before the 2 PM changeover. Also, the spare-parts guy said the new filter kit for the other cabinet is coming Thursday, so don't steal that one.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: No, don't just swap the MR-JE-AX196 amplifier right away. The manual lists amplifier malfunction as cause one, but the check order says disconnect U/V/W first and only replace the amplifier if the alarm persists. And on Line 3, check the motor-side U/V/W insulation before swapping the amplifier, because two of the last five AL.24 cases were wet motor terminal blocks.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: When you disconnect U/V/W for that test, tag the cables and wait 10 minutes after power-off before touching the terminals. Use a 500 V DC insulation tester on the motor, and treat a reading below 1 MΩ as a failed motor. Like I said about checking the motor side first, that's where I'd start.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Okay, but the motor power cable was replaced only 11 months ago. Shouldn't that be fine?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Don't skip the cable short check just because it's 11 months old. The manual puts that before the motor insulation check, so do it in order. Also, Cell F's cabinet fan filter is cleaned every 500 hours — a clogged filter has twice caused AL.24 by overheating the amplifier in summer.

turns.speaker: supervisor_01
turns.text: Good, and if you need a hand, Minh is back from lunch at 1. Let me know if the insulation tester is missing from the shop crib.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Hey, got a weird one on MR-JE-AX761 over the weekend. Operator Nguyen came in at 06:40 and the drive was showing F4.9 on the display. He hit reset, it cleared for about ten seconds, then came right back when he tried a home return.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: F4.9 is a home position return type warning. First thing, check what [Pr. PT45] is reading on the drive parameter screen. What's it showing?

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: It's reading 7. HMI shows the axis is not referenced either. Should I just swap out the amplifier? That's what I was thinking.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: No, don't replace the amplifier. The manual says F4.9 is a parameter setting range issue — you set the home position return type correctly and cancel with C ORST. Swapping the drive won't fix a bad parameter value.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Okay, so I'll just keep pressing C ORST until it clears then? The reset button on the panel cleared it once already.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: No, don't do that either. The manual is clear — the warning won't clear until the home position return type is set correctly. C ORST just cancels it after you fix the value.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Right. So on this cell what's a valid value for PT45?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: On this cell the valid range is 0 to 5. Value 7 showing up like that usually means the backup battery on the MR-JE-AX761 control board has dipped below 2.8 volts.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Battery causing a parameter to change? That's odd. We didn't log any parameter changes over the weekend.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Yeah, it happens. Before you change [Pr. PT45], measure the control board battery at CN4 with a multimeter. If it's below 2.9 volts, replace it — otherwise you'll be back here within two weeks.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Got it. CN4, under 2.9 replace. Anything else I should watch for?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Back in March 2023 we had a similar F4.9 on MR-JE-AX761. Turned out to be a loose CN4 connector after a panel cleaning, not the parameter value itself. So check that connector is seated properly too.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Loose connector, okay. So after I fix the value and the battery, can I just let it run the auto cycle?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: No, after restoring the correct home position return type, do a manual home return at low speed first. Make sure it references cleanly before you allow automatic cycle — otherwise you risk a crash at the hard stop.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Understood. Manual low-speed home return first. Hey, did you see the new shift schedule for next week? They moved us to 7 to 3.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Yeah I saw it. Not thrilled about the early start but it is what it is. Anyway, get that battery measured before lunch.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Will do. By the way, did the spare parts order for the other line come in? The one we placed last Thursday?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Not yet, delivery says Wednesday. I'll chase them if it doesn't show. Now, back to the MR-JE — like I said about the battery, don't skip that measurement. If you just set PT45 back to a valid value and the battery is weak, it'll drift again.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Right, measure at CN4 first. What value should I set PT45 to after?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Set it to whatever the original home position return type was for this cell — should be in the maintenance log. Just make sure it's between 0 and 5. Then C ORST to cancel the warning.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Okay. And if the battery reads fine and the connector is tight, then what?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Then you set the parameter and do the manual home return. But honestly, on this cell, nine times out of ten it's the battery. That's why I said check it before anything else.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Makes sense. I'll grab the multimeter and check CN4 now. Oh, and did you hear about the lunch truck? They changed the menu.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Yeah, someone mentioned that. Not sure I trust the new chili. Anyway, let me know what the battery reads.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Will do. I'll measure it and report back. Thanks for the help.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Hey, I need a hand. At 14:32 today the FX5-PLC495 in Palletizing cell E failed to pull recipe file LINE11_RCP.csv via FTPGET. It threw error code 41DFH. The weird thing is the same FTPGET was working fine earlier this morning.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: First thing, go check the SD card slot. Is the write protect switch ON?

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Yeah, I already looked. The write protect switch is in the ON position.

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: That explains it. On the FX5-PLC495, for FTPGET jobs always set the transferred file deletion setting to 'Not delete'. That avoids 41DFH when the SD card write protect switch is ON.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: But the deletion setting was already configured as 'Delete'. Did someone change it, or was it always like that?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: That switch was left ON after the March 2025 firmware update. Always check it first before any FTP transfer troubleshooting. It's bitten us before.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Okay so what do I do right now? Should I swap the SD card out?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: No, don't replace the card yet. 41DFH is the write protect switch being ON, not a card failure. Turn the switch OFF and retry the FTPGET once.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: And if it still fails after that?

turns.speaker: expert_01
turns.text: Then check for 41E4H. That one means the SD card access failed, so you'd recheck insertion, replace the card, or back up and initialize memory.

turns.speaker: junior_01
turns.text: Got it. And just to be safe, can I initialize the card myself if it comes to that?

turns.speaker: expert_01
